updateNotice.summary: CPIC announced a forthcoming change specific to rs75017182. Publication of the full updated guideline has not been verified in this build. No activity scores or dosing rules are applied.
updateNotice.captureStatus: Notice read online; direct archive retrieval returned HTTP 403. Summary is manually curated.

medications.name: Clopidogrel
medications.mechanism: CYP2C19 helps activate clopidogrel. Reduced function can mean less active drug, rather than slower clearance of the active medication.
medications.boundary: Guidance depends on a confirmed metabolizer category and the reason for treatment. The three marker calls do not establish that category.

medications.name: Omeprazole
medications.mechanism: CYP2C19 helps clear this medication. Reduced function may increase exposure; faster metabolism may decrease it.
medications.boundary: Interpretation needs confirmed phenotype, treatment indication and duration. Greater exposure is not necessarily safer.

medications.name: Dexlansoprazole
medications.mechanism: Its metabolism resembles lansoprazole, but direct genotype evidence is more limited.
medications.boundary: CPIC rates these recommendations as optional because direct evidence is limited.

medications.name: Esomeprazole
medications.mechanism: The guideline found inconsistent genotype–response evidence for this medication.
medications.boundary: No recommendation is not proof of no genetic effect, safety or suitability.

medications.name: Simvastatin
medications.mechanism: SLCO1B1 helps move simvastatin acid into the liver. Decreased transport can increase blood exposure and muscle toxicity risk.
medications.boundary: A single marker does not establish the full transporter phenotype or a personal risk estimate. Dose, other medicines and clinical history also matter.

medications.name: Fluorouracil
medications.locator: 2017 guideline · gene background and drug metabolism discussion, pages 1–3
medications.mechanism: DPD helps break down fluorouracil. Capecitabine is converted to fluorouracil. Reduced DPD activity can increase exposure and serious toxicity risk.
medications.boundary: Selected consumer calls do not establish DPD function, treatment suitability or a safe dose. No detected selected variant cannot rule out toxicity risk.
